source.version: Journal version of record: PNAS Nexus, 2025, 4, pgaf316, Research Report, advance access publication 28 October 2025 (received March 28, 2025, accepted September 11, 2025). Preprint at SSRN 5104064 (p. 10, Preprints).
source.title_on_document: Experimental evidence of the effects of large language models versus web search on depth of learning

supplement.where: "Supplementary material is available at PNAS Nexus online." (p. 10, Supplementary Material)
supplement.holds: Three preregistered replications whose results the main text does not report numerically (replication of experiment 1, n = 2,402, healthier-lifestyle topic with a third LLM + real-time web links arm; replication of experiment 1, n = 1,976, financial-scam topic; conceptual replication of experiment 4, n = 1,258); the experiment 2 mediation model; the ex post analysis controlling for number of websites visited; the full survey instruments and the GPT-4o prompts and stimuli for experiment 2. The main text prints arm means and F tests only, with no SDs or SEs, so any SDs would have to come from the supplement or the OSF data.

paper_design_summary: In three experiments (1 and 2 online on Prolific, 3 in a university lab), people were randomly assigned to learn about a topic from an LLM synthesis (in-house ChatGPT, a simulated ChatGPT page showing a GPT-4o summary, or Google AI Overview) or from Google web links, and then wrote advice for a friend on a separate page. The advice was scored with NLP tools for word count, named-entity references, and originality across writers (average pairwise cosine similarity of LDA topic vectors and average pairwise Levenshtein edit distance within condition). In experiment 4, 1,493 MTurk raters blind to condition rated pairs of experiment 3 advice texts for helpfulness, informativeness, trust, and willingness to recommend and adopt.

outcomes.name: Uniqueness of advice across writers (pairwise topical similarity and Levenshtein distance)
outcomes.question: after_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Average pairwise cosine similarity between all pairs of advice within each condition, computed on LDA topic distributions reduced with PCA (not neural embeddings). Convergent measure: average pairwise Levenshtein edit distance between all pairs of advice within each condition (lexical, character-level). Higher cosine similarity = less unique; higher edit distance = more unique.

contrasts.reported: cosine similarity: M_Google = 0.057, M_GPT = 0.159; F(1, 1,102) = 168.46, P < 0.001. Levenshtein edit distance: M_Google = 531.86, M_GPT = 481.59; F(1, 1,102) = 13.67, P < 0.001. Direction coded on diversity (sign reversed for cosine similarity): ChatGPT advice less diverse.

diversity_detail.metric: Average pairwise cosine similarity of LDA topic vectors (after PCA); average pairwise Levenshtein edit distance
diversity_detail.embedding_model: None; Latent Dirichlet Allocation topic model with principal component analysis
diversity_detail.computed_over: All pairs of advice within each condition
diversity_detail.uncertainty: One-way F test with df (1, 1,102), which matches one score per participant; how a per-advice score was formed from the pairwise similarities is not stated in the PDF
diversity_detail.notes: Paper frames these as originality or uniqueness of advice to the writer.

outcomes.name: Word count of advice
outcomes.question: after_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Number of words computed with LIWC 2022 (a count, not a creativity model)

outcomes.name: References to facts (unique named entities) in advice
outcomes.question: after_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: spaCy Named Entity Recognition count of words or word pairs in seven predefined categories plus a vegetable-gardening domain; paper labels it references to facts (unique entities)

contrasts.reported: unique entities: M_Google = 0.718, M_GPT = 0.464; F(1, 1,102) = 6.66, P = 0.010

data_and_code.data_url: OSF ("All relevant data, surveys, and preregistrations used in analysis can be accessed via OSF"; no URL given, p. 10)

eligibility.reason: Experiments 1-3 randomly assign individuals to learn from a generative-AI synthesis (ChatGPT, GPT-4o summary, Google AI Overview) vs. Google web links, then score the advice they write for originality across writers (pairwise cosine similarity and Levenshtein distance), which fits the codebook rule that writing tasks compared across writers for similarity belong. Analyzed samples are 1,104, 1,979, and 250 people. The AI was used in a learning phase and the advice was written afterward on a separate page, so all outcomes are after_ai and the comparison is ai_vs_active. A reviewer may question whether advice writing is a creative task and whether AI use for information gathering counts as AI assistance on the task.

one_line_finding: Advice written after learning from an LLM rather than web links was more similar across writers (pairwise cosine similarity 0.159 vs 0.057 in Exp. 1, 0.224 vs 0.072 in Exp. 2, 0.214 vs 0.073 in Exp. 3; all P < 0.001), shorter, and rated less helpful by recipients (3.553 vs 3.816, P < 0.001) (pp. 5-8).
open_questions: Is writing advice to a friend a creative task under the codebook, or does it qualify only through the across-writer similarity rule?

AI was used to learn about the topic and was not described as available while writing; outcomes are coded after_ai with timing immediate. In Experiment 3 the PDF does not say whether the Google tab stayed open during writing.
The diversity measures are computed over all pairs within each condition, yet tested with F(1, n-2), implying one score per participant; the per-advice score construction is not described in the PDF.
Experiment 4 choice proportions as printed are internally inconsistent: LLM-based advice 50.6% (n = 756) is called significantly lower than web-link advice 24.6% (n = 367). The labels look swapped.
Total sample: abstract says n = 10,462, introduction says n = 10,426 (p. 2).

Experiment 2: both arms saw GPT-4o-generated content (summary vs. GPT-4o-written article variants behind links), so the contrast isolates format, not AI content. Should it be ai_vs_active or ai_design?
No SDs or SEs in the main text; extraction will need the OSF data or the supplement.
notes: Only outcomes scored on the advice are listed. Not listed: self-reported learning, ownership, comprehensiveness, and effort items; search and writing time; Experiment 4 rating that 'less effort had been put into writing the advice' (M_standard-Google = 3.421, M_LLM-Google = 3.024; F(1, 1,492) = 94.471, P < 0.001, p. 8); the SEM in Fig. 3. Levenshtein edit distance is folded into each diversity outcome as a convergent variant (the paper calls it 'a convergent measure of the originality'), with both sets of numbers in 'reported'. Experiment 1 final sample is 53% female versus 46% at recruitment (p. 3). Supplementary studies S5 and S6 and the Experiment 4 replication (n = 1,258) have no results in this PDF; the Experiment 4 replication is not given its own study entry because it rates advice rather than assigning AI. Experiment 3 preregistration is not stated.
